# `liber:midi@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:midi` package (`midi.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem MIDI - MIDI 1.0 receive endpoints, as ordered bounded chunks with their host receipt time and cable, for components PermissionManager granted one endpoint.  THREE PARTIES. An ordinary client holds `midi`: it lists endpoints and can open nothing - receiving and sending each need a grant, and UMP is not supported at all yet. A client PermissionManager granted `midi-input` holds a receiver, and one granted `midi-output` a sender, minted through the private `midi-admin` for ONE endpoint of one publication and the life of one launched component. A PROVIDER - the USB MIDI class module, or the in-guest fixture - serves `liber:midi-device@1`, and MidiService is its one consumer.  SENDING IS THE SAME CHUNKS THE OTHER WAY. A sender hands over complete short messages and SysEx fragments under message numbers of its own choosing; MidiService checks and encodes them and answers once the device has taken them. There is no time to send AT - USB-MIDI 1.0 carries none - and no output scheduler.  CHUNKS, NOT MESSAGES. A chunk carries at most three MIDI bytes: a complete short message, a raw byte, or a FRAGMENT of a System Exclusive message - start, continuation, end, or start and end at once - under a per-cable message number. A consumer treats a SysEx as incomplete until the fragment that ends it, and discards it when an abort names it. Nothing assembles a whole SysEx: its cap, 64 kB with its delimiters, is enforced by counting.  ORDER AND TIME are `liber:event@1`'s: the endpoint's observation order across all its cables, never sorted, and host receipt time only - USB MIDI 1.0 carries no device timestamp, and none is invented.

## Interfaces

### interface `midi`

INVENTORY: the endpoints and what they are. `open` exists to say no precisely: receiving and sending each need a grant, a direction the endpoint does not have is invalid, and UMP is unsupported.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `endpoints` | `endpoints() -> result<list<midi-endpoint>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `open` | `open(endpoint: midi-endpoint-id, direction: midi-direction, protocol: midi-protocol) -> result<unit, error>` |  |

### interface `midi-input`

ONE RECEIVER, on the one endpoint this connection was minted for, for as long as its owner lives. Reads PULL: nothing is pushed into a client that is not reading.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `endpoint` | `endpoint() -> result<midi-endpoint, error>` |  |
| 2 | `read` | `read(max: u16, wait-ms: u32) -> result<midi-batch, error>` | At most `max` events, waiting at most `wait-ms` for the first; after the last event of an ended stream, the end. |
| 3 | `status` | `status() -> result<midi-receiver-status, error>` |  |
| 4 | `stop` | `stop() -> result<unit, error>` | Stop receiving; the queued events are discarded and the slot freed. |

### interface `midi-output`

ONE SENDER, on the one transmit endpoint this connection was minted for, for as long as its owner lives.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `endpoint` | `endpoint() -> result<midi-endpoint, error>` |  |
| 2 | `send` | `send(chunks: list<midi-chunk>) -> result<unit, error>` | Send these chunks, in order, as one batch: complete short messages, and SysEx fragments - three bytes each but the one that ends its message. CHECKED WHOLE BEFORE ANY OF IT IS SENT, and answered once the device has taken all of it; a refused batch sends nothing and leaves every open message as it was. |
| 3 | `stop` | `stop() -> result<unit, error>` | Stop sending; a message the sender left open stays unfinished, and the slot is freed. |

### interface `midi-admin`

THE MINTING ENDPOINT, PermissionManager's alone. The alias names a MIDI device the service's configuration binds to provider metadata; it resolves to exactly one current publication, and `endpoint` to one of its receive endpoints, or the mint fails. Minting starts the receiver; one receiver per endpoint.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mint` | `mint(alias: string, endpoint: u32, owner: handle<task>) -> result<midi-grant, error>` |  |
| 2 | `revoke` | `revoke(endpoint: midi-endpoint-id) -> result<u32, error>` | End every receiver on one endpoint; answers how many. |
| 3 | `mint-output` | `mint-output(alias: string, endpoint: u32, owner: handle<task>) -> result<midi-grant, error>` | The same for a SENDER on one transmit endpoint: one per endpoint, ended by close, revocation, owner death or device replacement. |
